methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two sets of information.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Implement a module with 8 D flip-flops
Each D flip-flop samples its corresponding data input d[i]
Sampling occurs on the positive edge of the clock clk
Flip-flops have a synchronous reset input
When reset is high, on the next positive edge of clk, the output q[i] will be set to zero
Input clk is a single bit input
Input reset is a single bit input
spec_atomic_units: Module has active-high synchronous reset input reset
When reset is high, output q is set to zero on the next positive edge of clk
Output q takes the value of input d on the positive edge of clk when reset is low
There is a setup time requirement for d and reset with respect to the positive edge of clk
There is a hold time requirement after the positive edge of clk
Output q is declared as a reg
Non-blocking assignments are used to update the value of q
Synchronous reset functionality is implemented using an if statement within the always block
